children: Inflation pressures broadened across the U.S. consumer price basket in October, with the weighted share of CPI components rising at an annualized pace above 2%, climbing to 76.3%, its highest level since August 2022.
The measure tracks the share of consumer price index components, weighted by their importance in the basket, whose month-over-month increases translate into an annualized rate above 2%.
The gauge climbed to 76.3%, up from about 70% in September, marking a notable reversal from recent months, when the measure hovered in the 60s and low 70s.
The increase suggested that price rises are becoming more widespread across CPI categories rather than being concentrated in a narrower set of components.
However, the measure captures the breadth of components recording increases above the 2% annualized threshold; it does not indicate how quickly overall consumer prices are rising.
